card.statement:
The most delicate relation to check is
$[E_{i},F_{j}]=\delta_{ij}H_{i}$ . Once this is proved, the so-called
Serre relation follows from it together with the integrability.

It is relatively easy to check the relation for $i\neq j$ . For the
proof of $[E_{i},F_{i}]=H_{i}$ , a key is to understand fibers of
projections $p_{1},p_{2}\colon\mathfrak{P}(V,W)\to{\mathfrak{M}}(V^{\prime},W),{\mathfrak{M}}(V,W)$ .
By (4.2), the fiber of $p_{2}$ at $[B,I,J]$ is isomorphic to the
projective space associated with the vector space
$\operatorname{Hom}((B,I,J),S_{i})$ , where $\operatorname{Hom}$ is the space of homomorphism as
framed representations. This is the first cohomology of the complex
(2.5) for $(B^{1},I^{1},J^{1})=(B,I,J)$ , $(B^{2},I^{2},J^{2})=S_{i}$ . As
we have remarked before, it is dual to the third cohomology of the
complex (2.5) with $(B^{1},I^{1},J^{1})$ and $(B^{2},I^{2},J^{2})$ are
swapped.
On the other hand, the fiber of $p_{1}$ at $[B^{\prime},I^{\prime},J^{\prime}]$ is isomorphic to
the projective space associated with
$\operatorname{Ext}^{1}(S_{i},(B^{\prime},I^{\prime},J^{\prime}))$ . This is the middle cohomology
of the complex (2.5) for $(V^{1},W^{1})=(S_{i},0)$ ,
$(V^{2},W^{2})=(V^{\prime},W)$ . Then one observes that the complex (2.5)
with $(V^{1},W^{1})=(S_{i},0)$ has the vanishing first cohomology group if
$(B^{2},I^{2},J^{2})$ satisfy the stability condition for $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}_{i}>0$ .
This is obvious as $0\neq\xi\in\operatorname{Ker}\alpha$ realizes $S_{i}$ as a
submodule of $(B,I,J)$ . Then $\zeta^{\mathbb{R}}(\dim S_{i})=\zeta_{i}^{\mathbb{R}}>0$
violates the stability condition.
Thus the difference of dimensions of the second and third
cohomology groups of (2.5) is the Euler characteristic of
(2.5), hence can be computed.
Now one uses that the Euler number of the complex projective space
$\mathbb{C}P^{n}$ is $n+1$ to complete the calculation.

paper.title: Introduction to quiver varieties -- for ring and representation theoriests
paper.abstract: We review the definition of quiver varieties and their relation to representation theory of Kac-Moody Lie algebras. Target readers are ring and representation theorists. We emphasize important roles of first extension groups of the preprojective algebra associated with a quiver.
